Microsoft Project

Microsoft Project supports task scheduling, resource planning and project tracking.

On the software discovery list. Connector development and release dates have not been announced.

Workflow ideas

Develop a project schedule

Start from the approved project dataset, calendar and reporting grain. In the intended Microsoft Project preview, develop a project schedule; the visible result is a structured planning or reporting view with source fields visible. Review data ownership, dates, relationships and completeness before accepting or exporting it.

Assign resources and baselines

Begin with the selected measures, activities, resources or work items. In the intended Microsoft Project preview, assign resources and baselines; the visible result is a decision view that exposes status, sequence and capacity. Review definitions, dependencies, resource limits and stale data before accepting or exporting it.

Review progress and variance

Use the current baseline, progress cut-off and governance rules. In the intended Microsoft Project preview, review progress and variance; the visible result is a reviewed forecast, report or delivery board with exceptions visible. Review variance, critical work, blockers and accountable ownership before accepting or exporting it.
